refinement.stopCriterion: Pass only when every observable category in every required view is acceptable, with no concrete discrepancies or revision instructions. Unobservable details are uncertain. This is an AI visual judgment, not measured accuracy or proof of quality improvement.

report.summary: The render retains the robot’s main parts, but differs in framing, head proportions, arm placement, and material visibility. Severe overexposure obscures several approved details.
revisionInstructions: Reduce camera magnification so the robot occupies approximately the reference’s central framing, with more space above and below. Match the reference’s elevated three-quarter angle and visible torso side.
Reduce the head relative to the torso and flatten its lower contour to match the reference’s rounded, slightly squat shape.
Move the arms upward toward the shoulders and match the reference’s compact peach oval shapes.
Reduce lighting intensity or exposure and adjust materials to restore the off-white head, muted turquoise body, peach arms and button, and dark gray eyes.
Preserve both eyes and the single chest button while restoring their clear contrast and the reference’s visible low-poly facets.

observations.detail: The robot fills substantially more of the frame, extending approximately from y=69–462 versus y=123–393 in the reference. The view also appears more frontal, with less torso-side visibility.
The head appears taller and larger relative to the torso, with a more spherical outline than the reference’s squatter head and flatter lower contour.
The arms sit lower relative to the head and shoulder junctions; their lower ends extend farther down the torso than in the reference.
Both eyes and the single chest button are present; no clearly missing or extra parts are visible. However, their contrast and the head’s polygonal facets are largely lost in the bright rendering.
The head and much of the torso and arms are nearly white from overexposure. The reference clearly shows an off-white head, muted turquoise body and feet, peach arms and button, and dark gray eyes.

report.summary: The render retains the robot’s main parts, but its framing, arm silhouette, and washed-out materials differ visibly from the approved reference.
revisionInstructions: Adjust the camera distance or orthographic scale so the robot occupies approximately the reference’s framing: head near 24% and feet near 77% of image height, rather than 14% and 91%. Preserve the elevated three-quarter viewing direction.
Reduce the arms’ outward bulk and bring them closer to the torso, especially the image-left arm, to reproduce the reference’s narrower silhouette and partial occlusion.

Restore the reference’s ivory head, turquoise torso and legs, peach arms and chest button, and dark gray eyes. Reduce lighting intensity or exposure to preserve these colors and visible surface shading.
Restore the visibly faceted surface treatment on the head and arms, and retain softly beveled torso and foot edges.

observations.detail: The arms create a wider, more outward-projecting silhouette, particularly on image-left. The reference’s arms sit closer to the torso. Camera framing is also substantially tighter: the rendered robot spans roughly 77% of image height versus 53% in the reference.
The arms appear bulkier relative to the head and torso, especially the image-left arm. The relative sizes of the head, torso, legs, and feet otherwise broadly follow the reference.

The head sits above the torso, both arms flank its upper sides, the button is on the chest, and two separated legs end in forward-projecting feet. The elevated three-quarter camera direction broadly matches.
Both oval eyes and the single round chest button are present. No concrete missing or extra feature is visible in this view; unseen rear details remain uncertain.

Strong highlight clipping makes the head, torso, and arms largely white. The reference clearly distinguishes ivory, turquoise, peach, and dark gray eyes. The render also loses the reference’s readable polygon facets, particularly on the head and arms.

refinement.error: Maximum revision cycles reached with unresolved discrepancies; no quality improvement is claimed.

interpretation: Real Codex and Blender outputs. Visual judgments are subjective; mesh hash differences prove a geometry change, not quality improvement.
